body.p: Claims 1-8 are pending in this application. By this Amendment, claims 1-7 are amended, and claim 8 is new. Support for the amendments to the claims may be found throughout the original application, for example, in [0012], [0015]-[0017], [0020], [0028]- [0029], [0032], [0038]-[0039], [0043]-[0053], [0059], [0061], [0063], [0064]-[0072], [0083]- [0084], and [0087]-[0088] and in Figs. 1, 3, 4, and 9-13. No new matter is added.
In view of the foregoing amendments and following remarks, reconsideration and allowance are respectfully requested.
I. Interview
The courtesies extended to Applicant's representative by Examiner Tu during the

telephone interview held September 18, 2024 are appreciated. The reasons presented during the interview as warranting favorable action are incorporated into the remarks below, which constitute Applicant's record of the interview. II. Claim Objections
The Office Action objects to claims 1 and 2 for an informality. Claims 1 and 2 are

amended. Specifically, in the amended Claims 1, 2, terms of the "first transition", the "second transition" and the "third transition" are introduced, and the "notification control" is specified in different cases by using these terms. Accordingly, as tentatively agreed during the interview, reconsideration and withdrawal of the objection are respectfully requested. III. Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. §101
The Office Action rejects claims 1-7 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 for allegedly being directed to non-statutory subject matter.
Claim 5 is rejected under section 101. Claim 1 is amended to recite "a cuff configured to surround a to-be-measured part" and the limitation is removed from claim 5.

Claim 1 is also amended to recite "the air system comprising at least a cuff configured to surround a to-be-measured part, a pump connected to the cuff via a first fluid pipe, and a valve connected to the cuff via a second fluid pipe."
The cuff, pump, and valve are substantive elements and not an abstract idea.

In addition, by reciting "to perform blood pressure measurement by driving the pump to feed an air to the cuff through the first fluid pipe to pressurize the cuff or driving the valve to exhaust the air from the cuff through the second fluid pipe to depressurize the cuff," the alleged abstract idea is integrated into a practical application.
Further, the alleged abstract idea is integrated into a practical application by the

recitation of "the processor is configured to act as:" "an air leakage testing unit ... to perform, during the blood pressure measurement to the second transition, air leakage testing on the air system"
In addition, the notification control is amended to include "when the air leakage
testing result is..." thereby integrating the alleged abstract idea into a practical application.
Accordingly, as tentatively agreed during the interview, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection are requested. IV. Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. §112(a)
The Office Action rejects claim 1 as failing to comply with the written description requirement under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a).
By this Amendment, claim 1 is amended to obviate the rejection and instead recite "in a second display mode more inconspicuous than the first display mode."

This is described in paragraph [0071] and shown in Figs. 15, 16. Another example of "in a second display mode more inconspicuous than the first display mode" is described in a paragraph [0076] and shown in Figs. 17A, 17C. In this example, as discussed during the interview, because ICl is blinking in Fig. 17A, ICl of Fig. 17C is more inconspicuous.
Accordingly, "inconspicuous" can be understood by a person skilled in the art based on the specification.
Accordingly, as tentatively agreed during the interview, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection are requested.
V. Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. §112(b)
The Office Action rejects claims 1, 2, 4, and 6 as being indefinite under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). By this Amendment, the claims are amended to obviate the rejection.

With respect to "the transition from the standby state to the power-off state," claim 1 is amended to recite ""a main control unit ...", "a first transition from a power-off state to a standby state in response to a power-on operation", "a second transition to the standby state after the blood pressure measurement", and "a third transition to the power-off state in response to a power-off operation in the standby state."

With respect to "degree of enhancement," claim 1 is instead amended to recite "in a second display mode lower in degree of enhancement than the first display mode", "in a second display mode more inconspicuous than the first display mode."
With respect to the indefiniteness rejection of claim 2, claim 2 is amended to recite "the first or third transition."

With respect to the indefiniteness rejection of claim 4, claim 1 is amended to recite "an air leakage testing unit to perform, during the blood pressure measurement to the second transition, air leakage testing on the air system." In conformity with this, the second paragraph (lines 2-3) of original Claim 4 is removed. Claim 4 now recites the air leakage testing on the air system is performed during the blood pressure measurement to the second transition.
With respect to the indefiniteness rejection of claim 6, "a message indicating a measure against the air leakage testing result" is changed into "a message notifying a
replacement of the cuff". An example of the "message notifying a replacement of the cuff" is described in a paragraph [0068] and shown in Fig. 14.
Accordingly, as tentatively agreed during the interview, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection are requested. VI. Claim Interpretation Under 35 U.S.C. §112(f)
The Office Action interprets claim elements as means-plus-function language under 35 U.S.C. §112(0.
While Applicant does not necessarily agree with this interpretation, by this Amendment, claims 1-7 amended to not invoke § 112(0.

Claim 1 recites a processor, wherein the processor is configured to act as... "a main control unit to perform ...", "an air leakage testing unit to perform ...", and "a notification control unit to perform ..." are recited.
Claims 4, 5, and 8 are similarly amended.
In addition, "a storage unit" and "a display device" are removed and specified as "a memory" and "a display", respectively.

Accordingly, as tentatively agreed during the interview, reconsideration and withdrawal of the means-plus-function interpretation are respectfully requested. VII. Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. §102 and §103
The Office Action rejects:
" claims 1 and 3-6 under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) over U.S. Patent Application Publication
" claim 2 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Mori in view of U.S. Patent Application
Publication No. 2010/0331709 ("Matsumura"); and
" claim 2 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Mori in view of U.S. Patent Application
Publication No. 2008/0319329 ("Tseng"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections.
By this Amendment, claim 1 is amended to recite: "the air leakage testing result

includes at least three air leakage levels..." and the notification control includes: when the air leakage testing result is..." As tentatively agreed during the interview, the asserted references do not teach or suggest at least this claim feature.
With respect to original claim 3 (portions of which are incorporated into proposed claim 1), the Office Action asserts that Mori teaches air leakage testing result includes three leakage levels.
Mori teaches:
" The first air leakage level indicates that an air leakage amount in the air system is smaller
than a reference value (an "unacceptable" leakage);
" The third air leakage level indicates that the air leakage amount is larger than a second
reference value greater than the first(an "acceptable" leakage); and
" The second air leakage level indicates that the air leakage amount corresponds to a value
between the first and second reference values (an "unacceptable" leakage). In contrast, in proposed claim 1 recites:
" The first air leakage level is an acceptable level- indicating that an air leakage amount is
smaller than a predetermined first reference value;
" The third air leakage level is a failure level, indicating that the air leakage amount is
larger than a second reference value set greater than the first reference value; and
" The second air leakage level indicates that the air leakage amount corresponds to a value
between the first reference value and second reference value.
Accordingly, Mori teaches only one acceptable leakage and two unacceptable

leakages. In contrast, in proposed claim 1, the first air leakage level is "acceptable", and the third air leakage level is "unacceptable". The second air leakage level corresponds to a level between the first air leakage level and the third air leakage level, that is, an initial stage where
air has just started to leak from the air systems. See paragraph [0059] of the present application.

Claim 1 further recites that the "notification control" is specified for different cases (i.e., during the first transition, in the standby state, during the blood pressure measurement and the second transition, and during the third transition) when the air leakage testing result is the second air leakage level. Mori et al. '950 (and the other cited documents) neither teaches nor suggests the "notification control" specified in the amended Claim 1.

For at least the foregoing reasons, the asserted references do not anticipate, and would not have rendered obvious claim 1. Claims 2-7 depend from claim 1 and, thus, also are not anticipated by and would not have been rendered obvious by the asserted references.
Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection are respectfully requested. VIII. New Claim

By this Amendment, new claim 8 is presented. New claim 8 depends from claim 1 and, thus, distinguishes over the applied references for at least the reasons discussed above with respect to claim 1, as well as for the additional features that it recites. Prompt examination and allowance of new claim 8 are respectfully requested.
IX. Conclusion
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that this application is in
condition for allowance. Favorable reconsideration and prompt allowance of the application are earnestly solicited.

Should the Examiner believe that anything further would be desirable to place this application in even better condition for allowance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the telephone number set forth below.
